description:
## Why this issue exists

Stoa has no account lockout after repeated authentication failures. An attacker can make unlimited password guesses against IMAP, JMAP, or the admin API with zero friction.

PCI-DSS 8.3.4 requires lockout after ≤6 failed attempts. HIPAA and SOC2 CC6.1 require equivalent controls.

## What needs to be done

- Add a failed-login counter table: `(user_id, window_start, fail_count)` in the stoa-mail Postgres schema.
- After N failures within a rolling window (configurable, default 6/15min), return 401/403 and set a lockout flag.
- IMAP AUTH failure path, JMAP API handler, and admin bearer handler must all increment the counter.
- Expose admin unlock endpoint.
- Write integration tests with ≥N+1 failed attempts to verify lockout triggers.
- Emit an `audit=true` tracing event on every lockout.

## Acceptance criteria

- 6 failed attempts within 15 minutes locks the account
- Subsequent attempts return failure without revealing lockout status
- Lockout clears after configurable timeout (default 30 min) or admin unlock
- All three auth surfaces (IMAP, JMAP, admin) are covered

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: PCI-DSS 8.3.4, HIPAA §164.312(d), SOC2 CC6.1.
title: Account lockout / brute-force protection
